text: 3:40 a.m. Taeo still hadn't answered Nib. Selling him would pay every bill. That was exactly what made it so hard to say no.
He stared at his family photo, then at the faded patch on his backpack. Across the room, Nib lay under his blanket, wide awake, watching him.
By morning, Taeo had already said yes to coffee with Dr. Pyo. He'd replied the minute the message came in.
He told Nib he didn't have to come. Nib was already at the door. If someone was buying him, he would be there.
At the tower by Hapjeong Station, Nib breezed through the revolving door. Taeo, running on no sleep, went around twice and bumped into the doorman.
Pyo greeted them warmly, with coffee and juice waiting. Nib checked the exits and took Pyo's seat against the wall.
Then he didn't even sit. He just wanted the view of the door. When Pyo offered him the juice, Nib said, 'You first.'
Pyo took a sip. Nib pushed the glass back anyway. Taeo whispered that it cost 13,500 won. Then Pyo could finish it, Nib said.
Pyo opened his folio. Nobody like Nib had walked into an assessment office in twenty years. At Kanghan Institute, he would get his own rooms, a garden, and a doctor.
And perhaps, one day, Kanghan could send him home. Could Pyo actually do that? Nobody could, yet. 'Then don't say perhaps.'
Pyo turned to Taeo. Wasn't that better than an eighteen square metre flat? Taeo couldn't deny it. And Nib heard every word.
Kanghan had studied arrivals before, Pyo mentioned. Taeo asked about those other arrivals. Pyo's smile froze for a beat. Arrival was an old category, he said. Kanghan was an old institute.
The deal: fifty million won for five years of exclusive observation, with Nib living at Kanghan. Taeo asked where Nib signed. He didn't. Taeo would.
Taeo looked up at Nib. Nib looked back and said nothing. This one was Taeo's call.
Taeo put down the pen and pushed the tablet back. No apology this time. 'He's not mine to sell.' Beside him, Nib's folded arms loosened.
Pyo took it calmly. The review was in twenty-three days. If the panel ruled Nib a construct, Kanghan wouldn't need Taeo's signature at all.
He left his card and walked out. Taeo had just turned down the price of five thousand lunches.
Nib drank the abandoned juice. It was already paid for.
Outside, they ran into Bae, the courier from the mart, steering his stone golem through a service door with three crates of juice.
Nib spotted it first. The bottom crate was splitting. He warned Bae, Bae yelled at the golem to stop, and the sudden halt burst the crate open.
Nib dove underneath and held it up until Taeo and Bae could lower it. Not one bottle broke. Bae called him a good spotter. Nib corrected him. A scout. Which was better.
Bae was still paying off that golem, 640,000 won a month. Broken bottles would have cost him a week's wages.
On the walk home, Taeo apologised for even considering the sale. Nib informed him that made five apologies today. He'd been counting.

That night, Chae confirmed the danger. A construct ruling would take the choice out of Taeo's hands. To prove Nib was a person, they needed proof that he chose his own work, and someone to vouch for him. Chae set up a meeting with Ryu Minho at the West practice yard.
Through the wall, Taeo told Nib he didn't have to come. A moment later, an amber pulse lit Taeo's palm. Nib had answered.
